notes: District-reported ('as censed by the districts') counts; the table total for chickens and rabbits is internally inconsistent; goat totals differ strongly from NISR AHS 2020. Older than 5 years (about 7 years): use for district proportions, not current counts.

claim: Napier (Cenchrus/Pennisetum purpureum): to 2,000 m, favoured above 1,500 mm; DM 2-10 t/ha/yr with no or inadequate fertiliser, 20-80 under high fertiliser; stem cuttings of 3+ nodes; cut every 6-8 weeks; fresh CP about 9.7% DM
title: Elephant grass (Pennisetum purpureum) datasheet
organization: Feedipedia (INRAE, CIRAD, AFZ, FAO)
notes: International reference, not Rwandan data; stunt disease is not covered on the page.

claim: Saban abattoir, 2017-18 festive period: nearly 600 goats and sheep slaughtered on Christmas Eve and Christmas versus about 300 on normal days; 'during these days people eat more goat meat than beef'; goat meat Rwf3,500/kg versus beef Rwf2,000/kg; Kicukiro abattoir closed 2017-11-23 leaving Saban the only abattoir in the city; staff buy livestock at markets across the country before holidays
title: Beef sellers eye more sales on New Year's Day
organization: The New Times (Rwanda)
notes: Older than 5 years; used for the festive pattern and the 2018 goat-meat price (Rwf3,500/kg). Page metadata shows a 1970 placeholder date in JSON but the meta tag shows 2018-01-01.

claim: Rugari Meat Processing (APTC, Ministry of Defence): abattoir with sections for cattle and goats; over 500 cattle and 700 goats at Gako (Bugesera) in 2016 with a target of 3,000 cattle and 10,000 goats by 2018; supplies 20 hotels and restaurants through outlets in Kigali, Rubavu and Rusizi; HACCP certification being pursued
title: Rugari moves to boost meat output, supply chain quality
organization: The New Times (Rwanda)
notes: Older than 5 years; current herd size, goat output and whether Rugari buys goats from outside suppliers are unknown.

claim: Veterinary AH Pharmacy Company Ltd, Kigali: sells essential veterinary medicines and microchip temperature sensors directly to smallholder farmers and offers a subscription livestock health-tracking app
title: Veterinary AH Pharmacy Company LTD (venture profile)
organization: VC4A (venture directory)
notes: Self-reported profile; no website, phone, email or address published; licence status not verified.

claim: Nyabihu: weekly Mukamira Livestock Market, buyers mostly from DR Congo; a sheep of 30-35 kg sells for Rwf100,000 (farmer quote); RAB imported 45 Merino ewes and 5 rams from Kenya, bred at RAB Gishwati station (143 animals after one year; 80 farmer applications, 60 approved); RAB built 15 livestock markets in the Southern, Western and Northern provinces; PRISM investment US$45.64 million; average Rwandan eats 8 kg of meat a year per RAB
title: Nyabihu's sheep market sees high demand from Congolese buyers
organization: The New Times (Rwanda)
notes: Single farmer quote for the price; the 8 kg meat consumption figure conflicts with 13-14 kg in LVS-08.

claim: Rwanda Council of Veterinary Doctors (RCVD) is the statutory veterinary body; address KG 569 St 1, Kacyiru, Kigali, P.o.box 2949; registrar named with a telephone line; website not listed
title: Veterinary statutory bodies (Rwanda entry)
organization: World Organisation for Animal Health (WOAH) Regional Representation for Africa
notes: Undated regional listing; contact line is the registrar's as printed. Email addresses are hidden on the page.

claim: Rural animal-health professionals are few and farmers pay vets for services; VSF Belgium and IMBARAGA supported 34 private vets and veterinary technicians (30 still active) in Huye, Nyanza and Nyamagabe in 2008-2019 with training and microcredit; vets and technicians set up surgeries, buy drugs and a motorcycle
title: Supporting Local Private Veterinary Services in Rwanda (factsheet)
organization: VSF Belgium (Vétérinaires Sans Frontières Belgium)
notes: NGO factsheet on Southern Province districts, not the candidate zones; used for how private vet services work (fee-for-service) only. Older than about 5 years for its figures.

claim: Station study of the productivity of the Small East African goat and its crosses with Anglo-Nubian and Alpine in Rwanda: traits examined were age at first kidding, kidding interval, litter size, mortality to 150 days, birth weight, litter weight and postpartum weight; no figures in the abstract and full text restricted
title: Productivity of the Small East African goat and its crosses with the Anglo-Nubian and the Alpine in Rwanda
organization: Tropical Animal Health and Production 20(4):219-228 (Wilson RT), record held by ILRI
notes: About 38 years old; abstract only (full text restricted); not Boer. The only Rwandan station-based goat productivity paper found.

claim: RAB service on IremboGov 'Purchase the Forage Seed': price depends on type and amount of seed; 7 days processing; applicant gives national ID or passport, contact details and an RCVD licence number, picks a pick-up station, receives a Bill ID after RAB's logistics officer approves, pays, then gets collection instructions; the page says the service enables private and public veterinarians to buy forage seed
title: How to Purchase the Forage Seed
organization: IremboGov support (Rwanda Agriculture and Animal Resources Development Board service)
notes: No seed species list, price list or station list on the page; whether farmers (not only vets) may apply is unclear. The IremboGov 'Agriculture' folder lists six services (VAT letter, NGO letter, bovine semen, livestock relocation, vaccines, forage seed) and none for buying breeding animals.

claim: MINAGRI ordered 70% of pastureland in Nyagatare, Gatsibo, Kayonza and Kirehe to be put under fodder crops and 30% under cow sheds (zero grazing for cows): fenced split, fodder storage required for dry spells, at least 5 improved dairy cows per ha in sheds, vaccination and insurance, water from rainwater harvesting or boreholes, one-year grace period, land to keep its pasture use when sold
title: Zero-grazing: Govt changes pastureland strategy in Eastern Province
organization: The New Times (Rwanda)
notes: Concerns cows in four named districts; goats, sheep, Bugesera, Ngoma and Rwamagana are not mentioned. Applicability to a small-ruminant farm: unknown.

claim: Kayonza (Gahini sector) dairy and fodder farm of 18 ha: two years without rain once forced herders to migrate; a 160 m solar-powered borehole cost Rwf80 million with a Rwf49 million government subsidy after the owner paid 30%; two lined dams of 960 m3 and rainwater tanks; fodder grown on 12 ha (Cameroon grass, Red Napier, Juncao grass, Chloris gayana, maize); hay, silage and sealed storage; 100 of a 300 t fodder target stored; hydroponic maize fodder
title: Rwanda: Kayonza Farmer Turns Arid Land Into Thriving Pasture
organization: allAfrica (Rwandan press report)
notes: One dairy farm, not goats; used for water-infrastructure cost and fodder-conservation practice in the Eastern lowlands.

claim: RAB plans to expand fodder land from 32,000 ha to 87,000 ha; improved forages (Chloris gayana, several Brachiaria varieties, Napier) rolled out in six districts including Bugesera, Nyagatare and Gatsibo; 31 legume and more than 20 cereal fodder varieties identified; farmer groups multiply fodder seed (one Nyagatare farmer on 1-3 ha with 33 farmers supplying fellow farmers and RAB); hydroponic fodder uses about ten times less water and takes 6-7 days; farmers trained in silage-making
title: How improved fodder is boosting milk production
organization: The New Times (Rwanda)
notes: Dairy-focused; no goat or sheep content and no seed prices.

claim: RAB researcher teaching bag silage, pit silage and hay making in Kayonza (using sorghum, maize, bean and rice straws, desmodium and calliandra leaves); in Murundi sector dairy output fell from 8,000 to 4,000 litres a day in the dry season; Eastern Province reports more than 10,000 livestock farms on about 100,000 ha
title: Why Eastern Province urgently needs zero grazing for livestock
organization: The New Times (Rwanda)
notes: Older than 5 years; cattle-focused.
